messages:
Avani: Quick follow-up from RFC review — we need to decide the SDK surface for paginated streams + retries across Python/TS/Go. High-level options: 1) expose opaque Iterator objects with resume() 2) expose resume_token in page/response 3) rely on transport-level session handoff.

Matt: +1 to keeping something language-native. In TS the async iterator idiom is common; token feels clunky.

Kevin: Go folks prefer explicit ResumeToken for deterministic replays. Iterators are fine but harder to serialize across processes.

Dee: Question: can we unify by making iterator carry an optional opaque token field that SDKs can serialize? e.g.

```
// TS
const it = client.listMessages();
const page = await it.next();
const token = it.getCheckpoint(); // optional string
```

Avani: That's the idea. But we need to think about retries: if transport transparently retries partial pages, token semantics must reflect "all items up to token consumed". Otherwise dedupe burdens user.

Matt: For HTTP transports we already have idempotency keys for unary calls. For paged streams we could attach a per-session id + offset in KV cache.

Kevin: Implementation concern: adding session state to servers increases memory/tracking. Alternative: server returns stable continuation cursor that encodes (session_id, offset) but is opaque.

Dee: I like server-provided cursor + client "hand-off" API. Eg `client.resumeFrom(cursor)` that returns a fresh iterator. That way each SDK maps cursor to idiomatic object.

Avani: Tradeoffs: server cursor = simplicity for client; but hard to support cross-version. We could version cursors and let server reject unknown versions with 400 + upgrade hint.

Matt: Retry behavior: define two modes — "at-most-once-per-item" (no dup) vs "at-least-once" (simpler). Default at-most-once preferable but more server complexity.

Kevin: If default is at-most-once we need server-side checkpoints flushed on responses which may increase tail latency.

Dee: Proposal: default at-least-once with client helpers for dedupe (client-side seenIds cache). Add opt-in header X-Session-Resume=stable for at-most-once with stronger SLOs.

Avani: Sounds reasonable. Action items: 1) Dee draft PR for SDK surface: iterator + getCheckpoint()/resumeFrom(cursor) across languages. 2) Matt/infra design server cursor format + versioning. 3) Kevin run perf sim on checkpoint flush costs.

Matt: I'll spin up a quick prototype in TS and post sample shape.

sre-bot: Deploy bot: no deploys in this thread.

Avani: Thanks all. If you have strong objections ping me; otherwise I'll add this to the RFC follow-up doc.
